messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: auto-dif Jacobians
parts:
I just added a function to compute Jacobians
via auto-dif. Given that the Jacobian is just a bunch of
gradients, it wasn't too hard. (Hessians are much
harder, as they involve second-order diffs we can't
handle yet, but we're on our way with the skeletal
forward auto-dif that's in place now -- once that's
built out, Hessians will also be easy.)

For Jacobians, I only needed to add a single function:

stan::agrad::zero_all_adjoints();

which walks over the expression stack and sets all
adjoint values to zero.

To get an idea how it works, here's a test case:

typedef stan::agrad::var AVAR;
typedef std::vector<AVAR> AVEC;

TEST(agrad_agrad,jacobian) {
AVAR x1 = 2.0;
AVAR x2 = 3.0;

AVAR y1 = x1 * x2;
AVAR y2 = x1 + x2;
AVAR y3 = 17.0 * x1;

AVEC x = createAVEC(x1,x2);
AVEC y = createAVEC(y1,y2,y3);

std::vector<std::vector<double> > J;
stan::agrad::jacobian(y,x,J);

EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(3.0,J[0][0]); // dy1/dx1
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(2.0,J[0][1]); // dy1/dx2

EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(1.0,J[1][0]); // dy2/dx1
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(1.0,J[1][1]); // dy2/dx2

EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(17.0,J[2][0]); // dy2/dx1
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(0.0,J[2][1]); // dy2/dx2
}

The jacobian() function is defined in agrad/agrad.hpp
and is defined using std::vector because agrad/agrad.hpp
has no dependencies on the Eigen matrix package.

In agrad/matrix.hpp, I'll include a second version that
populates an Eigen::Matrix. This will be a bit tighter in
memory and also let us calculate determinants.

I'd like to eventually let users specify arbitrary transformation
functions, then automatically handle the log absolute Jacobian
determinant for them.

I also moved some of the functions declared as
statics within the vari class to namespace-level functions.
There wasn't anything vari-specific in the implementation.

- Bob
